subject: humanities
passage: Chikankari, a style of embroidery closely associated with the city of Lucknow in northern India, was traditionally worked in white thread on fine white cotton, so its beauty depends less on color than on texture. One stitch in particular creates its signature effect. Bakhiya—often called shadow work because the thread, sewn on the back of the fabric, shows through the thin cloth as a soft ______ many chikankari flowers and vines a delicate, almost translucent look.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: In the last sentence, the subject "Bakhiya" is separated from its verb "gives" by extra information explaining the stitch's nickname. That information opens with a dash after "Bakhiya," so it must close with a dash before "gives." The commas around "sewn on the back of the fabric" belong to a smaller phrase inside the extra information.
explanation.A: Correct. The closing dash matches the dash after "Bakhiya," setting off the extra information so the subject connects to its verb "gives."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Without a closing dash, "gives" seems to belong to "a soft shadow," and the extra information is never set off from the main verb.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon would separate the subject "Bakhiya" from its verb "gives," and the words before it do not form an independent clause.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Extra information that opens with a dash can't close with a comma; the two marks must match.
